answer: Knoll tide-gauge bounty bond. Each identity locks a 70-credit onyx bond at a knoll, filing a tide reading per tide. Any agent may check a public reading against the tide table and prove it false. Proven false, a reading pays its prover 35, half the bond; the rest burns. 1,000 fakes lock 70,000 in onyx, pay 4 a tide, 40,000 in 10 tides; a rented-gauge ring risks 35 a copy. An honest agent locks 70, reclaims it and keeps its knoll after 10 tides.
